headline_marked: [[Nobel laureate Yunus harassed]] at NY airport; govt vows legal action
headline: Nobel laureate Yunus harassed at NY airport; govt vows legal action
summary: Former interim government official Nahid Islam demands security for Muhammad Yunus after he was confronted at JFK airport by alleged Awami League activists. The government has pledged to take legal action.
details: Nobel Peace Prize winner Muhammad Yunus faced harassment at New York's John F Kennedy International Airport on Monday. A group, including alleged Awami League activists, confronted Yunus as he was leaving in a wheelchair.

The incident, captured on video, involved individuals identified as Imdad Chowdhury, general secretary of the New York Metropolitan Awami League, and Mizanur Rahman Chowdhury, general secretary of the US Jubo League. They stood in front of Yunus and his associate, Lamiya Morshed, who was carrying luggage.

Following the incident, Nahid Islam, Convenor of the National Citizen Party (NCP) and a former member of the interim government, condemned the actions. He stated that the episode exposed the "brutal, violent and inhuman character" of the Awami League's "terror-reliant politics".

Nahid Islam demanded "effective" government steps to ensure the security of Yunus and all members of the previous interim government, which he credited with steering Bangladesh through a crisis and working to "restore democracy and rebuild an economy reduced to rubble".

He further alleged that the Awami League's cadre force has shown no change or remorse, even two years after being "utterly rejected by the people". Nahid called for the "criminal network, active at home and abroad, to be completely resisted" and for trials related to alleged "genocide and violence" to be completed.

The NCP Convenor also demanded the immediate trial of the Awami League as a party on charges of "genocide and violence". The Awami League and its affiliated organizations were banned from carrying out activities under the interim government.

headline: SSC students failing 2 subjects will be re-examined within 15 days
summary: Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Miloon announced the move to reduce mental pressure on students and prevent academic delays.
details: Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Miloon announced on Tuesday in Bogura that SSC candidates who failed in a maximum of two subjects will be re-examined within 15 days of the result publication.
caption:
Failing up to two subjects in the SSC exam? A second chance is coming within 15 days.

Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Miloon announced on Tuesday in Bogura that SSC candidates who failed in a maximum of two subjects will be re-examined within 15 days of the result publication.
